CVE-2026-91415, java-21-openjdk-headless 1:21.0.12.1.1-1.2.el9 in the Keycloak image: OpenJDK 2D font rendering flaw (CWE-787, out-of-bounds write); fix state: not-fixed. Grype rates it High; Red Hat CVSS 3.1 is 4.8 (preliminary) AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N, and the cve.org score is 7.0 with High availability impact. This package is the JVM that serves Keycloak's HTTP and it is loaded. Deployed context (#120, ADR-0018 D2): Keycloak is on the internal idp and pg-kc networks only; Caddy admits the LAN to /realms/decisya* and /resources/* on 8443 and the workstation to the admin paths on 8444, and port 9000 is never routed; the stack is not deployed today (#132, #29). Reachability: the flaw needs attacker-controlled font, text-layout or image data to reach the Java 2D APIs. The OTP QR code encodes a server-built otpauth URI into a bit matrix and writes a PNG, with no font or text drawn and no image decoded, and usernames are admin-made (registrationAllowed false, editUsernameAllowed false); /resources/* is served to the browser as bytes; there is no upload that parses graphics on the LAN paths; the realm has no identity provider and no SMTP server; the stack's bind-mount table admits no provider or theme JAR; KC_FEATURES is not set; the admin console is on 8444, workstation-only, and needs authentication with OTP. Void if any of these change: Keycloak's networks, its mounts, KC_FEATURES, the realm's identity providers or SMTP. Keycloak is on the request path of a LAN-reachable service, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: issue #190, approved by Marco 2026-10-24; added 2026-10-24, expires 2026-11-02, 9 days. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-114406, ca-certificates 2025.2.80_v9.0.305-91.el9 in the Keycloak image: root certificates that signed eMudhra intermediates with weak keys; fix state: not-fixed. Grype rates it Critical; Red Hat CVSS 3.1 is 6.8 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N. Java's cacerts on this image derives from this system store, and Keycloak trusts it as a TLS client (KC_TRUSTSTORE_PATHS adds the Caddy root to it and does not replace it); browsers do not use this store. Deployed context (#120, ADR-0018 D2): Keycloak is on the internal idp and pg-kc networks only; Caddy admits the LAN to /realms/decisya* and /resources/* on 8443 and the workstation to the admin paths on 8444, and port 9000 is never routed; the stack is not deployed today (#132, #29). Reachability: Keycloak's only outbound TLS peer is the back-channel logout call to the app host, which resolves to Caddy's fixed address on the internal idp network; JDBC to Postgres is plaintext on the internal pg-kc network, so no CA store is involved; the realm has no identity provider, no SMTP server and no client JWKS URL; Keycloak has no network with egress. A man in the middle needs a position on idp, which holds only Caddy and Keycloak (both with all capabilities dropped, NET_RAW included), or root on the Docker host, and either is already a compromise of the identity tier. Void if either of these changes: any egress network for Keycloak, or any outbound peer outside idp and pg-kc. Keycloak is on the request path of a LAN-reachable service, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: issue #190, approved by Marco 2026-10-24; added 2026-10-24, expires 2026-11-02, 9 days. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-91403, java-21-openjdk-headless 1:21.0.12.1.1-1.2.el9 in the Keycloak image: the OpenJDK CA store trusts roots that signed eMudhra intermediates with weak private keys (CWE-295); fix state: not-fixed. Grype rates it Critical; Red Hat CVSS 3.1 is 6.8 (preliminary) AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N. This package is the JVM that serves Keycloak and it is loaded. Its default trust store is the system ca-certificates store (Red Hat's statement for the RHEL OpenJDK RPMs), which holds the same roots as CVE-2026-114406. The pinned image still carries the unfixed ca-certificates 2025.2.80_v9.0.305-91.el9, so Red Hat's remedy is not present in the image and this entry rests on reachability alone. Keycloak trusts the store as a TLS client (KC_TRUSTSTORE_PATHS adds the Caddy root to it and does not replace it); browsers do not use this store. Reachability: Keycloak's only outbound TLS peer is the back-channel logout call to the app host, which resolves to Caddy's fixed address on the internal idp network; JDBC to Postgres is plaintext on the internal pg-kc network, so no CA store is involved; the realm has no identity provider, no SMTP server and no client JWKS URL; Keycloak has no network with egress. A man in the middle needs a position on idp, which holds only Caddy and Keycloak (both with all capabilities dropped, NET_RAW included), or root on the Docker host, and either is already a compromise of the identity tier. Void if either of these changes: any egress network for Keycloak, or any outbound peer outside idp and pg-kc. CVE-2026-111497, brotli-libs 1.2.0-r1 (Alpine apk) in the Postgres image: Grype rates it Critical; Alpine fix 1.2.1-r0. The latest official 18-alpine rebuild (sha256:10a5c69a8303, pushed 2026-10-26) does not carry the fix, so ADR-0015 item 3 applies while the tag resolves to this digest; the pin was moved to it under a one-off cooldown waiver for pin currency recorded by Marco on 2026-10-26 (#195), which fixes nothing. Reachability (apk info -r and ELF scan, docker run --network none, 2026-10-26): brotli-libs is needed only by libcurl (apk info -r brotli-libs lists libcurl-8.22.0-r0 only); libcurl is needed only by the libpq OAuth client module (the only file linking libcurl.so is /usr/local/lib/libpq-oauth-18.so); the postgres server binary links neither libcurl nor brotli (ldd). No connection in the repository uses an OAuth parameter (no oauth_issuer or oauth_client_id as a connection parameter). Postgres sits on internal networks only (pg-kc and pg-app), and the stack is not deployed today (#132, #29). Void if the server or any library it loads links libcurl or brotli, or if any connection uses OAuth. Ends when the tag is rebuilt with the fix; bump the digest then; not renewed past 2026-11-02 without a new issue and a fresh G3. Issue #195, approved by Marco 2026-10-26; added 2026-10-26, expires 2026-11-02, 7 days.

GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q (CVE-2026-116587), github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 in the Caddy binary: denial of service when parsing JWKs that contain RSA keys (High, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). No fixed v3 release exists (fix state: not-fixed, v3.0.5 is the latest); v4 is raised to 4.1.6 under ADR-0021 item 3 (#212). Remove when a fixed v3 or a Caddy release without v3 exists. Component path: caddypki, then smallstep authority, then go.step.sm/crypto/jose, linked into the binary. Class (b), the vulnerable path is not reachable in the deployed configuration (G3 ruling 1, #212): `tls internal` signs a certificate request made in-process, with no token and no JWK from a peer; Caddy's internal issuer builds the smallstep authority with no provisioners, and only the acme_server directive configures provisioners, which the Caddyfile does not use; the admin API is off; every site uses the internal issuer only; no other standard module verifies JOSE. Void at once, whatever the expiry, if any of these changes: an acme_server directive or a pki CA other than the implicit local one; the admin API turned on in any form; a TLS issuer other than internal, or Caddy as an ACME client; a module added to the build that verifies JWS or JWT or fetches a JWKS. Impact if a premise failed: availability only, on the LAN edge before authentication. Caddy is the LAN edge, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: approved by Marco 2026-10-29; added 2026-10-29, expires 2026-11-12, 14 days (approved under the ADR-0015 item 4 bound; from #225 an ADR-0021 item 7 exception for a finding with no fix). A renewal needs a new issue, a fresh G3 and a fresh approval.
